chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about salat al-khawf (the prayer of fear). He said:

The Imam stands, and a group from his companions comes and stands behind him, while another group faces the enemy. The Imam leads them in one rak'ah, then he stands and they stand with him; then he remains standing while they perform the second rak'ah. Then some of them give salam to one another, then they depart and take the place of their companions, and the others come and stand behind the Imam. He then leads them in the second rak'ah, then the Imam sits, and they stand and perform another rak'ah; then he gives salam to them, and they depart with one taslim.

He said: And in the Maghrib prayer it is similar to that. The Imam stands and a group comes and stands behind him; then he leads them in one rak'ah. Then he stands and they stand; the Imam remains standing while they perform the two rak'ahs, recite the tashahhud, and some of them give salam to one another. Then they depart and stand in the position of their companions, and the others come and stand behind the Imam. He leads them in one rak'ah in which he recites, then he sits and recites the tashahhud, then he stands and they stand with him, and he leads them in another rak'ah. Then he sits, and they stand and complete one more rak'ah, then he gives salam to them.

key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the prayer leader who organizes and leads the alternating groups
key_terms.الْعَدُوِّ: the enemy whom one group remains positioned against
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبِ: the sunset prayer consisting of three rak'ahs
key_terms.تَسْلِيمَةٍ: a single act of concluding the prayer with salam
key_terms.صَلَاةِ الْخَوْفِ: the prayer performed in conditions of danger or battle
key_terms.طَائِفَةٌ: a group or contingent from the companions
key_terms.يَتَشَهَّدُونَ: they recite the tashahhud while seated in prayer

ai.seo_question: How is salat al-khawf performed behind the Imam according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal method of performing salat al-khawf under conditions of danger, with one group praying behind the Imam while another remains facing the enemy, then alternating positions. It also details how the same arrangement is adapted for Maghrib prayer, showing the jurisprudential structure of congregational worship during military threat.
